title: Schedule of Tax Refund Offset Figures — Benefit Overpayment Accounts
content:
Collections applies the following figures by classification when it refers debts on Benefit Overpayment Accounts to the Treasury Offset Program or for a state income tax refund intercept.

| Classification | May be referred to the Treasury Offset Program | May be intercepted from a state income tax refund | Smallest balance that may be referred (USD) | Calendar days without any recovery, and with no current plan, after which the debt is delinquent for referral | Calendar days between the notice of intent and the referral | Calendar days between the notice of intent and a state tax refund intercept |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Non-Fraud Overpayment — Agency Error | No | No | 25.00 | 90 | 60 | 30 |
| Non-Fraud Overpayment — Employer Reporting Error | No | No | 25.00 | 90 | 60 | 30 |
| Non-Fraud Overpayment — Appeal Reversal | No | No | 25.00 | 90 | 60 | 30 |
| Non-Fraud Overpayment — Claimant Error | Yes | Yes | 25.00 | 90 | 60 | 30 |
| Fraud Overpayment — First Offense | Yes | Yes | 25.00 | 90 | 60 | 30 |
| Fraud Overpayment — Repeat Offense | Yes | Yes | 25.00 | 90 | 60 | 30 |

## Notes

1. The three classifications marked No in both eligibility columns are never referred, and the notice, delinquency and minimum-debt figures shown for them have no effect.
2. The state tax refund intercept notice period of 30 days is shorter than the Treasury Offset Program notice period of 60 days.
